name: Lūipa

realization_account.text: A prince (of Oḍḍiyāna in some accounts) who left his kingdom, and on a ḍākinī's rebuke for his remaining pride lived twelve years on the Ganges bank in Bengal eating the fish entrails thrown away by fishermen; attained mahāmudrā; converted King Dārika and his minister Ḍeṅgi; root guru of the Cakrasaṃvara lineage that bears his name and poet of the first Caryāgīti song. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 1): As honey smeared on the nose of an untamed wild dog makes it bite in all directions, the guru's instruction given to the dull and unfit burns their own mind-stream; the fortunate who realize the unborn destroy concepts at the mere meeting with appearances, as a sword tied to the trunk of a steady, maddened elephant routs an army.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Līlapa

realization_account.text: A king who would not give up his throne and pleasures; a guru taught him to meditate while seated on his lion throne, taking the jewel of his ring (or his royal ease) as the object, and he attained realization in the midst of royal life. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 2): In the hermitage of the four immeasurables the king of yogins is like a lion, his head adorned with a turquoise five-braided mane, bearing the yogin's insignia of the five families; as the lion's ten claws tear the flesh and bones of elephants, the yogin's ten perfections tear apart concepts, the adverse side; realizing thus, Līla was freed.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Virūpa
alt_names: Śrī Dharmapāla (monastic name, per Tibetan accounts)

realization_account.text: A monk-scholar (at Nālandā or Somapura) who recited the Vajravārāhī (or Cakrasaṃvara) mantra for twelve years without a sign and threw his rosary into the latrine; that night Nairātmyā appeared and gave him consecration; he ate pigeons and drank wine and was expelled, walked across the Ganges, stopped the sun to go on drinking without paying, and subdued non-Buddhist shrines; his Hevajra teaching is the source of the Sakya Path and Result. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 3): Within mahāmudrā, rest that innate, beyond thought and reasoning, in its own selfless state; it does not fall into annihilation, being self-known in experience; it does not fall into permanence, being without clinging: it is union.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Ḍombipa (Ḍombi Heruka)

realization_account.text: A king of Magadha, disciple of Virūpa, who took a low-caste ḍombī girl as his consort; banished, he lived with her in the forest for twelve years and returned riding a tigress, holding a snake as whip; author of Hevajra works and (traditionally) the Sahajasiddhi. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 4): As the power of an alchemical elixir turns iron into gold, the power of the precious consecration transforms the afflictions into non-dual gnosis.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Śavaripa
alt_names: ri khrod pa / sha ba ri pa (Tibetan)

realization_account.text: A hunter of the mountains of eastern India who, with his two wives Lokī and Guṇī, was shown by Avalokiteśvara (in the guise of a hunter who killed with a single arrow) the hell awaiting a killer; he renounced hunting and, instructed in mahāmudrā, attained realization; guru of Maitrīpa. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 5): In the forest of ignorance roam the deer of grasped and grasper; drawing the bow of means and wisdom I shot the single arrow of the essential meaning: what died was conceptual thought, its flesh I ate as non-duality, its taste I experienced as great bliss, and the fruit, mahāmudrā, was attained.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Saraha
alt_names: the Great Brahmin (bram ze chen po)

tradition.text: the first of the human mahāmudrā teachers; placed by some Tibetan histories before Nāgārjuna

realization_account.text: A brahmin of eastern India who kept Buddhist practice secretly and drank liquor; expelled from caste, he took as his consort a low-caste arrowsmith woman who taught him through her work; he sang dohās to the king, the queen and the people who came to condemn him, and they became his disciples; in another story he meditated twelve years and then asked for the radish curry his consort had made before he entered samādhi. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 6): Kye ho, friends! That innate is not found elsewhere; it is found from the mouth of the true guru. If the essence of the ultimate is realized, the mind knows no death and the body no destruction.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kaṅkaripa

realization_account.text: A householder of low caste whose beloved wife died; grieving in the cremation ground, he was taught by a yogin to see her as the ḍākinī, empty and self-appearing, and realized mahāmudrā. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 7): As in empty space, the form free of one and of two — the self-appearing gnosis consort — is beyond example and beyond all conventions.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Mīnapa

realization_account.text: A fisherman swallowed by a great fish; in its belly on the ocean floor he overheard the god Śiva (Maheśvara) teaching Umā the secret yoga and practised it for twelve years before being freed; his feet sank into rock when he danced. Widely identified with Matsyendranātha of the Nāth tradition (identification disputed). Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 8): The fisherman holding his hook was carried by karma into the ocean; relying on the body of the great fish, he practised the great god's instruction, and his qualities became famed as more than earth and stone could bear.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Gorakṣa

realization_account.text: A cowherd boy who, at Mīnapa's request, guarded and served the limbless Cauraṅgi for twelve years; received the instruction and attained realization; the tradition says he did not die. Identified with Gorakṣanātha of the Nāth tradition. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 9): Whether one's birth is high, middling or low, when the cause meets strong conditions the fruit of unceasing karma is wondrous: loving service done for Cauraṅgi was the cause, by that condition the seed of the elements grew; through Matsyendra the deathless nectar was made firm; Gorakṣa saw non-dual reality — the wondrous king of the three worlds.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Cauraṅgi

realization_account.text: A prince falsely accused by his stepmother, whose hands and feet were cut off and who was left in the forest; Mīnapa taught him breath and meditation, Gorakṣa served him, and after twelve years his limbs were restored. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 10): Through long beginningless existence the roots of the tree of ignorance, well moistened by the water of formations, spread the many limbs of existence; that great tree of ignorance Cauraṅgi felled with the axe of the true guru's instruction and the three wisdoms.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vīṇāpa

realization_account.text: A prince devoted to playing the vīṇā; his guru taught him to meditate on the sound of the lute without discursive thought, and through sound he realized the unborn. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 11): Examining with devotion and diligence the sound to which one has grown habituated in error, examining sound as unborn, Vīṇāpa realized selflessness.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Śāntipa (Ratnākaraśānti)

realization_account.text: A great scholar of Vikramaśīla invited to Siṃhala; returning, he met Koṭali, a peasant digging the mountainside to whom he had once given instruction, and found that Koṭali had realized it while he had not; he then practised twelve years and attained the fruit. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 12): As a child nourished by its mother grows to a wrestler's strength, one of small mind, gradually raised by the guru's instruction, becomes of the great vehicle; as medicines cure the diseases of wind, bile, phlegm and their combination, the guru's instruction burns in an instant the clinging to 'I' and self.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Tantipa

realization_account.text: An old weaver neglected by his family, living in a hut behind their house; Jālandhara, passing, taught him to see his weaving as the path, and he attained realization in old age. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 13): Worldly weavers weave all their threads into cloth; by my guru's instruction all phenomena are woven: the emptiness of the five gnoses is the thread, the instruction the comb, wisdom the frame, and they are woven into the dharmakāya in which space and awareness are not two.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Camaripa

realization_account.text: A cobbler taught by a monk-yogin to treat his work — the leather, the awl, the thread — as the path, who realized while making shoes. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 14): This leather of conceptual signs, soaked in the vessel of vajra emptiness, is stretched and stitched by the experience of wisdom in the continuous abandoning of the eight worldly concerns; the maker of the shoe of the spontaneous dharmakāya is Camaripa, best of cobblers.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Khaḍgapa

realization_account.text: A thief who, taught by a yogin, circumambulated an image of Avalokiteśvara and gained the siddhi of the sword; he then turned it to the deathless sword of gnosis. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 15): The worldly armed hero, though he fights enemies and battles without end, himself falls under suffering; with the sword of deathless gnosis Khaḍgapa defeated the enemies of the three realms and enjoys the fruit.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Nāgārjuna (the siddha)

tradition.text: the Madhyamaka master, who lived some six hundred years

realization_account.text: Ordained at Nālandā, he mastered alchemy, fed the saṅgha in famine by turning iron into gold, received the Prajñāpāramitā from the nāgas, and in the end gave his own head to a prince; the tradition identifies him with the Madhyamaka master and with the author of the Pañcakrama. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 16): One who has not realized should not engage in the (special) conduct: if he does, it is like a kingdom seized by its subjects; one who has realized should not act like one who has not: if he does, it is like an elephant caught in a swamp.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kāṇhapa (Kṛṣṇācārya)

realization_account.text: A monk-yogin of Somapura, disciple of Jālandhara, of great powers and great pride; the lives tell of his pride being humbled and of his death by a woman's curse; author of the Yogaratnamālā, of dohās and of many Caryāgīti songs. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 17): As a chariot lacking one wheel cannot go even when pulled, so, though one strives in giving and the other perfections, without a guru there is no supreme siddhi; as vultures of perfect strength with spread wings cut through the sky, fortunate yogins who have taken the instruction of consecration to heart are blissful.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Karṇaripa (Āryadeva)

realization_account.text: Born from a lotus in Siṃhala, disciple of Nāgārjuna at Nālandā; gave one of his eyes to a woman (or tree-goddess) who asked for it — hence 'the one-eyed'; defeated non-Buddhist debaters; the tradition identifies him with the Madhyamaka Āryadeva and the author of the Caryāmelāpakapradīpa. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 18): All buddhas of the three times are one in essence; realized, that is one's own mind by nature; wishing to realize it, leave it uncontrived just as it is; habituated to it, yoga becomes manifest.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Thaganapa

realization_account.text: A compulsive liar taught by a monk to meditate that all appearances are a lie; he realized emptiness through his own habit. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 19): As water in the ear is drawn out by water, so, meditating on the false appearances of existence as false, one sees the truth.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Nāropa

realization_account.text: A great scholar and gatekeeper of Nālandā (or Vikramaśīla) to whom a ḍākinī appeared as an old woman and asked whether he understood the words or the meaning; he left to seek Tilopa, underwent twelve great hardships and received the whole transmission; teacher of Marpa and of the six dharmas. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 20): As a universal monarch with his armies rules the continents and subcontinents, the yogin of the one taste of the innate rules saṃsāra: that is great bliss.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Śalipa

realization_account.text: A low-caste man terrified by the howling of wolves (jackals) near the cremation ground where he lived; a monk taught him to meditate on all sounds as the howl, and through the fear itself he realized. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 21): Skilled painters paint a very terrifying image; seeing it they themselves grow afraid; examined, it is an unestablished image that appears.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Tilopa

realization_account.text: A brahmin who served as a royal priest, then became a monk and yogin; lived as a sesame pounder and as servant to a courtesan in Bengal; by the Tibetan account received the four instruction lineages from Caryāpa, Nāgārjuna, Lavapa and Sukhasiddhi and directly from Vajradhara; guru of Nāropa. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 22): A bird on the slope of Mount Meru appears golden by the mountain's nature; the wise, realizing the unborn, let go of things: great bliss.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Catrapa

Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 23): For the yogin whatever appears is instruction; seeing the unborn is the supreme master; for the childish there is the concept that grasps two, and from it the fruits of virtue and evil arise as two.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

realization_account.text: A proud brahmin obsessed with purity who was taught by a yogin to overcome his pride and disgust. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 24): Realizing the meaning of emptiness pacifies error; meditating on love perfects conduct; by habituation to the non-duality of the manifold, the adverse is realized as one taste, the fruit.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Dukhaṇḍi

realization_account.text: A scavenger who stitched rags; taught the generation and completion stages. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 25): Meditate on the conventional generation stage and the ultimate completion stage in union as mahāmudrā: the fruit, the three bodies and gnosis, dawns.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Ajogipa

realization_account.text: An idle son who would do nothing but lie in bed; a guru taught him to visualize a drop (like a mustard seed) at the tip of his nose while lying down, and he realized. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 26): By the true guru's instruction I meditated on a drop at the tip of the nose, the upper door; my mind steady in it, the object, the mustard-seed drop, was lost in emptiness.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

realization_account.text: A handsome man thought mad by the people; taught to use his condition as the path. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 27): These beings have been deluded since beginningless time, and so the whole world is uneven; the nectar medicine of the guru's instruction burns the diseases of delusion in a single instant.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Dhobīpa

realization_account.text: A washerman taught to see his washing as the purification of mind. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 28): Though one washes it for a long time, charcoal does not turn white by nature; the nature, wholly pure emptiness, is pure; the guru's instruction is the best washer of the nature.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 28 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A washerman taught to see his washing as the purification of mind.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. The washing imagery confirms the identification with Abhayadatta's washerman.

name: Kaṅkaṇa

realization_account.text: A king who meditated on the light of the jewel of his bracelet (kaṅkaṇa) as the light of mind. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 29): From the wish-fulfilling jewel of thought the colour of experience arises; by the power of conduct all needs and wishes come; it is accomplished by those who have equal taste.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Kambala (Kambalapāda, Lvabapa)

realization_account.text: A prince who became a monk and then a yogin wearing only a black woollen blanket; he defeated a band of witches (ḍākinīs) who stole it; teacher of Indrabhūti, author of the Navaślokī and a Cakrasaṃvara commentary; named in Tilopa's Ṣaḍdharmopadeśa as the source of dream yoga (as La ba pa). Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 30): In the deep and vast ocean full of jewels the nāga kings enjoy themselves marvellously; likewise all appearances and sounds are primordially the dharmakāya, and for those with realization the enjoyment is marvellous.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Ḍeṅgipa

realization_account.text: A brahmin minister who, with his king (Dārikapa), became a disciple of Lūipa and was sold as a servant to a courtesan, threshing rice for twelve years; he realized in that service. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 31): If horses and elephants are like the ocean, there is great bliss; if monkeys and children are like drawings on water, they are concepts; if river, sun and medicine are alike they are not divided; by crest, eye and wheel the fruit is gained.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Bhandepa

realization_account.text: A god (or wealthy man) who, envying a yogin's radiance, was taught the four immeasurables. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 32): Love without clinging is supreme; realizing the natural state is compassion; uncontaminated bliss is joy; all phenomena one taste is equanimity perfected.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 32 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A god (or wealthy man) who, envying a yogin's radiance, was taught the four immeasurables.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. The song recasts the four immeasurables in terms of realization.

name: Tandhepa

realization_account.text: A gambler who lost everything and was taught that the three realms are as empty as his purse. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 33): As the many recollections and awarenesses are exhausted and cease in the non-conceptual expanse, so all phenomena of appearance and existence are exhausted and cease in the expanse of emptiness.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 33 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A gambler who lost everything and was taught that the three realms are as empty as his purse.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Identification with Abhayadatta's Tandhepa is by position only (low).

name: Kukkuripa

realization_account.text: A brahmin yogin who, on pilgrimage, rescued a starving bitch and practised in a cave with her; invited to Indra's heaven he returned for the dog, who was revealed as a ḍākinī; associated with the Mahāmāyā tantra and poet of Caryāgīti songs; in Tibetan accounts one of Marpa's teachers. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 34): Worship of buddhas and the like brings no benefit; where there is desire and striving there is no buddha; the glory of experience is the true guru's blessing; the fortunate have it within themselves yet do not see it.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kucipa

realization_account.text: A farmer with a goitre on his neck whom Nāgārjuna taught to visualize the growth enlarging and then to see it as empty. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 35): Where the innate is concerned, if one strains, a thorn arises; if one lets go without clinging, that is the supreme meditation; by the light of the guru's speech the extremes of existence and non-existence are not found; what is not found is seen; realizing that is the supreme meaning.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Dhamupa (Dhāma?)

realization_account.text: Not identified with certainty: Tōh 2292's 'Dhamu' may be Abhayadatta's Dharmapa (36) or the Caryāgīti poet Dhāmapa. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 36): From duality comes the poison of ignorance, which constantly seizes arisen awareness; the light of the guru's speech clears the poison-disease of the delusion of appearance and existence.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Mahipa

realization_account.text: A wrestler proud of his strength, taught to wrestle with his pride. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 37): The pride of ignorance obscures the wish-fulfilling jewel of non-conception; in wishing to act, needs and wishes arise; it is accomplished by those who have equal taste.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Acinta

realization_account.text: A poor woodcutter consumed by desire for wealth, taught to meditate on his longing as the sky. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 38): In objectless mahāmudrā the many deluded recollections are lost; by the light of gnosis-awareness whatever appears is seen as mahāmudrā.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Bhalaha

realization_account.text: Not well recalled; identification by position only. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 39): Bliss, bliss — the bliss of no-thing; without clinging, the bliss of no-thing; knowing all imputations there, bliss; the secret that needs no accomplishing, bliss.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 39 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). Not well recalled; identification by position only.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Nalina

realization_account.text: A poor man or prince who was taught to meditate on the lotus; low certainty. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 40): In the petalled lotus at the crown the moving seed is joy; drawing out the essence is supreme joy; the innate, beyond joy, the unsurpassed, is attained.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 40 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A poor man or prince who was taught to meditate on the lotus; low certainty.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Refers to the joys of the completion stage (restricted domain); summarized only.

name: Bhusuku

realization_account.text: A monk of Nālandā who did nothing but eat, sleep and stroll (bhu-su-ku); challenged to recite a text before the assembly he recited the Bodhicaryāvatāra and rose into the air; Abhayadatta identifies him with Śāntideva; also a poet of the Caryāgīti. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 41): Until one realizes oneself there is great difference between tastes, and saṃsāra and the buddhas are very different; at the time of realization saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are great bliss, like a jewel blazing in the ocean.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Indrabhūti

realization_account.text: King of Oḍḍiyāna (Sambhola), brother of Lakṣmīṅkarā, who practised while ruling and attained realization; author of the Jñānasiddhi. Several Indrabhūtis are distinguished in Tibetan histories (the king who received the Guhyasamāja from the Buddha, the siddha, and a 'younger' one). Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 42): If the moments of time are not blessed, the yoga of outer and inner conduct does not reach completion; the nature of joy and bliss is no different from the buddhas; when clinging is released, the experience of the innate is supreme joy.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Mekopa

realization_account.text: A food seller who fed a yogin daily and received instruction; afterwards he wandered the cremation grounds with a terrifying stare. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 43): First realize your own mind from the true guru; then make all appearances undivided; habituated to non-duality, dwell in the cremation ground; having realized equality, practise the observance of madness.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Koṭali

realization_account.text: A peasant digging a mountainside with a hoe whom Śāntipa taught to dig the mountain of mind; he realized before his teacher did. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 44): All pleasure and pain arise from mind; by the guru's instruction dig the mountain of mind; the wise may dig mountains of earth but will not gain innate great bliss; ordinary knowing awakens in the centre of the heart and in the six collections bliss is unbroken; all imputations are meaningless causes of suffering; rest in the innate state beyond meditation and non-meditation.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kamparipa

realization_account.text: A blacksmith taught to visualize his forge within: the channels as bellows and the fire of gnosis. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 45): On the hearth of natural form, on the charcoal of recollection, awareness and concepts, blowing the bellows of lalanā and rasanā and kindling the fire of gnosis in the avadhūtī, the concepts of the three poisons are forged into the dharmakāya; realizing this, Kampari was freed.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Smith imagery confirms the identification.

name: Jālandhara

realization_account.text: A brahmin who, in a cremation ground, received the Hevajra (or Saṃvara) instruction from a ḍākinī; guru of Kāṇha and Tantipa; identified with the Nāth Jālandharanātha (Hāḍipā). Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 46): All the many recollections, awarenesses and concepts of the three realms, of body, speech and mind — why not bind them by blessing into lalanā, rasanā and avadhūtī?
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Rāhula

realization_account.text: An old man despised by his family, taught to meditate on Rāhu swallowing the moon. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 47): The good outer Rāhu devoured the light of the moon non-dually; the drop of the conventional moon is devoured non-dually by the Rāhu of expanse and awareness.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Dharmapa

realization_account.text: Abhayadatta's 'eternal student' (a scholar who went blind?) or the Caryāgīti's Dhāmapa; identification uncertain. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 48): Into the vessel of the phenomena of appearance and existence pour the butter of bodhicitta; on the wick of the six consciousnesses kindle the fire of non-dual gnosis: the darkness of conceptual delusion is destroyed.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Dhokaripa

realization_account.text: A pot-bearer who carried a pot everywhere; taught to see it as the vessel of dharmadhātu. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 49): Into the vessel of the nature of dharmadhātu put the substance of awareness, the dharmakāya; the fruit of expanse and awareness together fortunate yogins realize by awareness.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Medhina

realization_account.text: A tireless farmer taught while working the fields. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 50): By the wisdom of innate awareness and by means stained with afflictions, from the ground, the natural state, the fruit — spontaneous great bliss — is realized.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Paṅkaja

realization_account.text: A brahmin 'born of a lotus' who worshipped Avalokiteśvara and was taught by Nāgārjuna. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 51): As long as one is not held by a guru and does not realize, a wish-fulfilling jewel and a glass bead are the same; held by the guru and by realization, they are as the light of sun and moon to a firefly.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Ghaṇṭāpa

realization_account.text: A royal monk-scholar of strict celibacy whom the king of Pāṭaliputra tried to shame by sending a young woman; he took her as consort and, when accused, the two rose into the sky as Cakrasaṃvara and Vajravārāhī; founder of the Ghaṇṭāpa lineage of Cakrasaṃvara (the five-deity body maṇḍala). Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 52): The three — lalanā, rasanā and avadhūtī — the guru blessed and bound; the three — self, mind and appearance — the wise make firm so that realization may arise.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Jogipa

realization_account.text: A low-caste man sent by Śavaripa on pilgrimage to the twenty-four sacred sites, reciting the mantra as he walked. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 53): By habituation to a mind subtle and clear like the flame of a lamp, all things stable and moving dissolve into dharmadhātu.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Caluki

realization_account.text: A drowsy man who could not stay awake; taught to meditate with his sleep. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 54): By long habituation to the true guru's instruction, earth and the other elements dissolve into awareness and self-appearance becomes mahāmudrā.

name: Gorura

realization_account.text: A bird-catcher taught to see his snares and the birds as mind. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 55): All outer and inner phenomena are gathered in mind; realizing mind itself as clear, the four modes of conduct are the dharmakāya; realization made manifest is complete buddhahood.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Lucika

realization_account.text: A man who wished to escape saṃsāra; taught to cross by the guru. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 56): Having wandered long in the ocean of saṃsāra since beginningless time, today by the supreme boat, the true guru, I crossed the ocean hard to cross.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Niguṇa

realization_account.text: A lazy, 'qualityless' son of a householder, taught that his idleness could be the path. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 57): Having shown the experiences like waves on water, enter conduct by means; by the true guru's instruction the concepts of desire and hatred are made into their own nature.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Jayānanda

realization_account.text: A brahmin minister who fed crows secretly and was imprisoned; low certainty. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 58): The samādhi of gnosis-awareness is without beginning and abides as the innate; realized as it is, it is certain; conceptual recollection itself is darkness.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Pacari

realization_account.text: A pastry-maker who offered his cakes to Avalokiteśvara; low certainty. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 59): Look nowhere; look in the middle; supreme joy and the joy of cessation are great bliss; having spoken the power of the mantra's secret, the signs of yoga should be made nine(?).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Campaka

realization_account.text: A king of Campaka who delighted in the scent of flowers; taught to meditate on the flower's fragrance. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 60): For means and wisdom, which are like clear light, the stream of the guru-river pervades all; from the wish-granting tree of the innate the fruit, the three bodies, is self-clear and wholly complete.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 61): In the unsurpassed cremation ground, the great place of awakening, the hard path of union and great bliss was shown; the supreme yogin, a lord free of emblems, realized that by the kindness of the guru's instruction.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Kumaripa

realization_account.text: A potter taught to see the wheel and kiln as the path. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 63): By the wheel of karma consistent with its cause the many songs and dances of existence are made; by the fire of gnosis-awareness every stain of delusion is burned.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 63 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A potter taught to see the wheel and kiln as the path.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Tōh 2292 reads 'kaM pa la'; the wheel-and-fire imagery fits Abhayadatta's potter (63).

name: Dhūmapa

realization_account.text: Known only from Tōh 2292, in the position where Abhayadatta has Carpaṭi. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 64): The supreme vow of all mantra practitioners is not to cling to one's own realization; filled with the realization of innate mind — that is seeing all the buddhas.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 64 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). Known only from Tōh 2292, in the position where Abhayadatta has Carpaṭi.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Maṇibhadrā

realization_account.text: A young wife of a householder who received instruction from Kukkuripa and practised secretly for a year while keeping house; when she broke her water pot on the way home she realized, and later flew into the sky. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 65): When one is without concepts, the many concepts follow sound; therefore the nature becomes manifest: whatever appears is that nature itself.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 65 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A young wife of a householder who received instruction from Kukkuripa and practised secretly for a year while keeping house; when she broke her water pot on the way home she realized, and later flew into the sky.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. The second line is uncertain.

name: Mekhalā

realization_account.text: The elder of two sisters of Devīkoṭa, mocked in marriage, who took instruction from Kāṇha; when he asked for a fee, the two sisters cut off their heads and offered them, and sang their realization; he restored them; they are linked to the 'headless' Vajrayoginī (Chinnamuṇḍā). Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 66): All outer and inner are gathered in mind; without clinging there is equal taste; without striving, the supreme meditation; non-dual great bliss is complete buddhahood.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 66 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). The elder of two sisters of Devīkoṭa, mocked in marriage, who took instruction from Kāṇha; when he asked for a fee, the two sisters cut off their heads and offered them, and sang their realization; he restored them; they are linked to the 'headless' Vajrayoginī (Chinnamuṇḍā).
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Kanakhalā
alt_names: nA ga ka la ka (Tōh 2292 spelling)

realization_account.text: The younger of the two headless sisters (see Mekhalā). Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 67): Putting on the great armour, with jewel-like courage, launching the boat of one's own mind, one surely enters the interior of the picture.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 67 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). The younger of the two headless sisters (see Mekhalā).
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Tōh 2292 reads 'nA ga ka la ka'; identified with Kanakhalā by position (low). The song's meaning is obscure.

name: Kalakala

realization_account.text: A man who talked incessantly and was shunned; taught to hear all speech as echo. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 68): In the centre of the pure sky of dharmadhātu the thunder of the unborn resounds; all the deluded phenomena of appearance and existence are the beautiful fruit, the three bodies and gnosis.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 68 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A man who talked incessantly and was shunned; taught to hear all speech as echo.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Kantali

realization_account.text: A ragman or tailor who pricked his finger; taught to see needle, thread and cloth as the path. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 69): With the needle of the true guru and the thread of compassion I stitched the three realms into a garment: wondrous yogin of cloth!
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 69 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A ragman or tailor who pricked his finger; taught to see needle, thread and cloth as the path.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Needle-and-thread imagery fits the tailor.

name: Dhahuli

realization_account.text: A rope-maker with blistered hands. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 70): Union-awareness, the treasury of jewels, the non-dual state, is not found by seeking; like a mind that has given up activity, as it is placed, so it is blissful.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 70 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A rope-maker with blistered hands.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Udhili

realization_account.text: A man who wished to fly like the birds; he gained the power of flight. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 71): Following after others, yogins go astray; do not let go of unrelated habits(?); do not abide anywhere; it is not something to be sought elsewhere.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 71 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A man who wished to fly like the birds; he gained the power of flight.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Two lines are uncertain.

name: Kapālapa

realization_account.text: A father whose sons had died; he carried a skull in his grief and was taught by Kāṇha to meditate on the skull and bone ornaments as symbols. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 72): All things are the non-dual Vajradhara; ornaments, the skull and the rest are adventitious; the delusion of grasping 'I', too, is not found when one searches for it oneself.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 72 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A father whose sons had died; he carried a skull in his grief and was taught by Kāṇha to meditate on the skull and bone ornaments as symbols.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Kirapala

realization_account.text: A conquering king who repented after seeing the grief of the women of a sacked city. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 73): Until realization one is bound by the concepts of self and other; when realization comes, self and other are not established; so what is called 'buddha' is one's own (nature): hold that, free of elaboration, uncontrived, in its own place.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 73 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A conquering king who repented after seeing the grief of the women of a sacked city.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Sakara (Sāgara)

realization_account.text: A prince born from a lotus (Dowman's 'lotus child'); identification of Tōh 2292's 'pa ga ra' with him is by position. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 74): Beings tormented by suffering were given a rain of desirable things; so at the great place of suchness, pressing the nāga king of awareness, the rain of secret-mantra awareness fell on the fortunate male and female vidyādharas.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 74 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A prince born from a lotus (Dowman's 'lotus child'); identification of Tōh 2292's 'pa ga ra' with him is by position.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Sarvabhakṣa

realization_account.text: A glutton with a belly like a pot whom Saraha taught to visualize his stomach empty as space and consuming the sun and moon. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 75): When not realized there is great difference among tastes; realized, tastes have no difference in essence; likewise when not realized saṃsāra and nirvāṇa appear different; realized, saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are great bliss.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 75 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A glutton with a belly like a pot whom Saraha taught to visualize his stomach empty as space and consuming the sun and moon.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Nāgabodhi

realization_account.text: A thief who came to rob Nāgārjuna and became his disciple (the 'red-horned thief'); he is counted in the Ārya Guhyasamāja lineage and is said to live on at Śrīparvata. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 76): Dwelling on earth, all is good fortune; gone to the ocean's depths, one is free of poverty; sword in hand, great enjoyment; gone to no particular direction, one meets one's friends.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 76 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A thief who came to rob Nāgārjuna and became his disciple (the 'red-horned thief'); he is counted in the Ārya Guhyasamāja lineage and is said to live on at Śrīparvata.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. The images may name siddhis (earth, ocean, sword); uncertain.

name: Dārikapa

realization_account.text: A king of Pāṭaliputra who, with his minister Ḍeṅgi, became Lūipa's disciple and served a temple courtesan for twelve years; a lineage holder of Lūipa's Cakrasaṃvara and a Caryāgīti poet. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 77): Great bliss is within oneself but unrealized, obscured by delusion; one who wants bliss and clarity should gather the accumulations of merit and gnosis; without the two accumulations, though one strives for a hundred lives, without a guru one will not realize great bliss.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 77 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A king of Pāṭaliputra who, with his minister Ḍeṅgi, became Lūipa's disciple and served a temple courtesan for twelve years; a lineage holder of Lūipa's Cakrasaṃvara and a Caryāgīti poet.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Putali

realization_account.text: A mendicant who carried a painted image (of Hevajra) on his back; identification of Tōh 2292's 'su ta ba' with him is by position. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 78): Everything is the nature of the sugatas; abandoning the wrong paths set up by the intellect and striving on the path of the essence, the fruit of the essence is certain; whoever, from the true guru, has the consecrations together with the innate pervades all with its taste — Vajradhara seals (all) with the unborn.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 78 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A mendicant who carried a painted image (of Hevajra) on his back; identification of Tōh 2292's 'su ta ba' with him is by position.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Panaha

realization_account.text: A bootmaker; low certainty. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 79): Contemplating the meaning of the innate essence, as one contemplates so one realizes; therefore it abides at ease and all one wishes arises freely.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 79 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A bootmaker; low certainty.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Kokilipa

realization_account.text: A pleasure-loving king who, disturbed by the song of the cuckoo (kokila), was taught to meditate on sound. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 80): Giving up activity is the instruction; being without clinging and craving is the realization; the bliss of no-thing is the meditation; when there is nothing to accomplish, that is the supreme fruit.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 80 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A pleasure-loving king who, disturbed by the song of the cuckoo (kokila), was taught to meditate on sound.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Anaṅgapa

realization_account.text: A handsome man vain of his looks, taught to see the body as illusory. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 81): Saṃsāra has no essence; in this rainbow-like body, by ignorance, clinging and pride, one holds poison as bliss; when the poison-disease of clinging is cleansed, saṃsāra itself is the dharmakāya.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 81 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A handsome man vain of his looks, taught to see the body as illusory.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Lakṣmīṅkarā

realization_account.text: Princess of Oḍḍiyāna, sister of Indrabhūti, promised in marriage to a king of Laṅkāpurī; she refused, feigned madness, lived in the cremation grounds and attained mahāmudrā; she taught the king's sweeper (who became a siddha); author of the Advayasiddhi; originator of a lineage of the 'headless' Vajrayoginī. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 82): First, the intelligent generate realization; second, they meditate undistractedly on the natural state; then, when experience has arisen, they practise conduct with care.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 82 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). Princess of Oḍḍiyāna, sister of Indrabhūti, promised in marriage to a king of Laṅkāpurī; she refused, feigned madness, lived in the cremation grounds and attained mahāmudrā; she taught the king's sweeper (who became a siddha); author of the Advayasiddhi; originator of a lineage of the 'headless' Vajrayoginī.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Tōh 2292's 'nI lak+Sha na' at position 82 is taken as Lakṣmīṅkarā (low). The song states a sequence of view, meditation and conduct.

name: Samudra

realization_account.text: A pearl-diver; low certainty. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 83): Realizing the unborn but lacking experience is like an ogress carrying a child in her hand; not separated from experience and the natural state, that too is like an elephant entering a pond.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 83 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). A pearl-diver; low certainty.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292. Whether the second image is praise or warning is unclear.

name: Vyāli

realization_account.text: An alchemist who sought the elixir of immortality; a courtesan found it for him; low certainty. Realization song in Tōh 2292 (no. 84): Seeing the true guru one sees reality; meditating in the openness of the sky is the supreme solitude; fully realizing phenomena there is nothing adverse; drinking the milk of the sky one lives.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: No. 84 of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292 order). An alchemist who sought the elixir of immortality; a courtesan found it for him; low certainty.
notes: Life from Abhayadatta's Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti recalled from memory (not read locally); the song is read locally in Tōh 2292.

name: Vajradhara
summary: The 'holder of the vajra', the primordial or sixth buddha in whose form the Buddha teaches the tantras; the ultimate source of the tantric lineages and the form in which the guru is to be seen (Gurupañcāśikā 22).

name: Maitrīpa (Advayavajra)
summary: U44 contribution: Indian scholar-siddha (c. 1007–1085), disciple of Śavaripa (and in some accounts of Nāropa), said to have been expelled from Vikramaśīla for keeping wine and a consort; author of the some twenty-one short works of the Advayavajrasaṃgraha (amanasikāra, the four seals, the Tattvaratnāvalī) and of a Vajrayoginī sādhana lineage; teacher of Marpa and of Vajrapāṇi and Sahajavajra.

name: Niguma
summary: Kashmiri yoginī (c. 10th–11th c.), in Tibetan accounts Nāropa's sister or consort, who taught Khyungpo Naljor the six dharmas that bear her name and the mahāmudrā of the 'amulet box'; source of the Shangpa Kagyu.
notes: Her 'six dharmas' and the Shangpa details belong mainly to U46.

name: Sukhasiddhi
summary: Yoginī of Kashmir who, per the Shangpa account, became a siddha late in life under Virūpa; named in Tilopa's Ṣaḍdharmopadeśa (Tōh 2330) as the source of the instructions on the intermediate state and transference.

name: Buddhaguhya
summary: Indian master of the kriyā, caryā and yoga tantras (8th c.), author of commentaries on the Mahāvairocana and the Tattvasaṃgraha (Tantrārthāvatāra); invited to Tibet under Trisong Detsen but declined, sending a letter.

name: Buddhajñānapāda

realization_account.text: After years of practice he had a vision of Mañjuśrī, who gave him the oral instruction on the two stages.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Founder of the Jñānapāda school of the Guhyasamāja (late 8th c.); trained under Haribhadra in Prajñāpāramitā and had a vision of Mañjuśrī, who gave him the teaching (tradition); teacher of Dīpaṅkarabhadra; associated with the early years of Vikramaśīla under King Dharmapāla.
notes: Place names and teachers recalled with low confidence.

name: Dīpaṅkarabhadra
summary: Disciple of Buddhajñānapāda and author of the Guhyasamājamaṇḍalavidhi.

name: Vitapāda
summary: Commentator in the Jñānapāda tradition (on the Mukhāgama and the Samantabhadra sādhana).

name: Candrakīrti (the tantric)
summary: Author of the Pradīpoddyotana on the Guhyasamāja; the tradition identifies him with the Madhyamaka Candrakīrti, disciple of Nāgārjuna; scholars place him c. 9th–10th c.
notes: Homonym: tch:candrakirti (the Madhyamaka author, U40) is kept separate by the scholarly account; the tradition identifies them.

name: Śākyamitra
summary: Commentator on the Tattvasaṃgraha (Kosalālaṃkāra) and member of the Ārya Guhyasamāja circle (Pañcakrama chapter traditions).

name: Vilāsavajra
summary: Author of the Nāmamantrārthāvalokinī on the Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti (8th c.?).

name: Ānandagarbha
summary: Great exegete of the yoga tantras (c. 9th c.), author of the Tattvālokakarī on the Tattvasaṃgraha and of works on the Sarvadurgatipariśodhana.

name: Padmavajra
summary: Author of the Guhyasiddhi, first of the seven siddhi texts; possibly the same as Saroruha(vajra), author of a Hevajra sādhana.

name: Anaṅgavajra
summary: Author of the Prajñopāyaviniścayasiddhi; disciple of Padmavajra per the siddhi-text lineage.

name: Sahajayoginīcintā
summary: Yoginī author of the Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasiddhi.

name: Vajragarbha
summary: U44 contribution: in the Hevajra the bodhisattva who questions the Buddha; the Hevajrapiṇḍārthaṭīkā, one of the three 'bodhisattva commentaries' of the Kālacakra circle, is ascribed to him.

name: Puṇḍarīka
summary: Second kalkin king of Śambhala in the tradition's account, son of Mañjuśrīyaśas, author of the Vimalaprabhā and the Paramārthasevā; historically the Vimalaprabhā dates to c. 1030–1050.

name: Mañjuśrīyaśas
summary: First kalkin king of Śambhala who united the castes into one vajra family and composed the abridged Kālacakra (Laghutantra), by the tradition's account.

name: Sucandra
summary: King of Śambhala who requested the Kālacakra from the Buddha at Dhānyakaṭaka and wrote it down as the Mūlatantra (the tradition's account); regarded as an emanation of Vajrapāṇi.

name: Kālacakrapāda
summary: The name of the Indian masters (an elder and a younger) credited with bringing the Kālacakra from Śambhala to India in the early 11th c. and teaching it at Nālandā/Vikramaśīla; Tibetan histories connect them with Cilupa and Piṇḍo; details differ by account.

name: Abhayākaragupta
summary: U44 contribution: abbot of Vikramaśīla (d. c. 1125), author of the Vajrāvalī, Niṣpannayogāvalī and Āmnāyamañjarī, which standardized the maṇḍala and consecration rites of late Indian Vajrayāna.

name: Vibhūticandra
summary: Indian master of the six-branch yoga (c. 1200) who fled to Nepal and Tibet after the fall of the monasteries; source of a six-branch lineage.

name: Śākyaśrībhadra
summary: The Kashmiri paṇḍita (1127/1140s–1225) who went to Tibet in 1204 after the destruction of Vikramaśīla, giving ordination and Kālacakra transmissions.

name: Atiśa Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna
summary: U44 contribution: Bengali master of Vikramaśīla (982–1054) who received tantric teachings from many siddhas (Avadhūtipa, Ḍombi, Nāropa per accounts); in the Bodhipathapradīpa (vv. 64–67) he permits the master's consecration but, citing the Ādibuddha tantra, forbids the secret and wisdom consecrations to celibates.

name: Jayabhadra
summary: Early Cakrasaṃvara commentator of Vikramaśīla (Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā), c. 9th–10th c.

name: Bhavabhaṭṭa
summary: Commentator on the Laghuśaṃvara (Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā/Vivṛti), c. 10th c.

name: Durjayacandra
summary: Commentator on the Cakrasaṃvara and Hevajra (Kaumudī), c. 10th c.; teacher of Drokmi's circle per Tibetan accounts.

name: Munidatta
summary: Author of the Sanskrit commentary on the Caryāgīti (c. 13th c.?).

name: Abhayadatta
summary: Compiler of the Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti, the lives of the eighty-four siddhas (c. 11th–12th c.); often identified with Abhayadattaśrī of Campāraṇya.

name: Vīraprabhāsvara
summary: Compiler of the realization songs of the eighty-four siddhas (Tōh 2292), named in its colophon as 'slob dpon dpa' bo 'od gsal'.
notes: Sanskrit form of the name reconstructed by the unit.

name: Tripiṭakamala
summary: Author of the Nayatrayapradīpa (c. 10th–11th c.?) setting out the superiority of the mantra way.

name: Kuladatta
summary: Author of the Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā (11th–12th c.).

name: Vāgīśvarakīrti
summary: Vikramaśīla 'gatekeeper' (11th c.), author of the Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśa and of works on the Guhyasamāja and consecration.

name: Śūnyasamādhipāda
summary: Author of the Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi.

name: Sahajavajra
summary: Disciple of Maitrīpa, author of the Tattvadaśakaṭīkā on 'mahāmudrā joined with the pāramitā view'.

name: Vajrapāṇi (the Indian master)
summary: Disciple of Maitrīpa (b. 1017), who taught mahāmudrā in Nepal and Tibet and translated Saraha's Queen Dohā with Asu (colophon of Tōh 2264).
notes: Distinct from the bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.

name: Aśvaghoṣa (author of the Gurupañcāśikā)
summary: The author named in the colophon of the Gurupañcāśikā ('mahācārya Aśvaghoṣa'); the scholarly account distinguishes him from the classical poet.

name: Lalitavajra
summary: Siddha of Oḍḍiyāna credited with bringing the Vajrabhairava tantra from the ḍākinī land (tradition).

name: Śubhakarasiṃha
summary: Indian master (637–735) who brought the Mahāvairocana Sūtra to China and translated it with Yixing (724).

name: Vajrabodhi
summary: South Indian master (671–741) who brought the Tattvasaṃgraha (Vajraśekhara) tradition to China; teacher of Amoghavajra.

name: Amoghavajra
summary: U44 contribution: disciple of Vajrabodhi (705–774), translator of the first part of the Tattvasaṃgraha and of many kriyā texts into Chinese.

name: Cāṭila
summary: Siddha-poet of the Caryāgīti: poet of Caryāgīti 5 (the bridge over the river of existence).
notes: Song numbers recalled from the standard edition (Shastri/Kvaerne); not read locally.

name: Ḍheṇḍhaṇa
summary: Siddha-poet of the Caryāgīti: poet of Caryāgīti 33 (the riddle song).
notes: Song numbers recalled from the standard edition (Shastri/Kvaerne); not read locally.

name: Guṇḍarī
summary: Siddha-poet of the Caryāgīti: poet of Caryāgīti 4.
notes: Song numbers recalled from the standard edition (Shastri/Kvaerne); not read locally.

name: Mahīdhara
summary: Siddha-poet of the Caryāgīti: poet of Caryāgīti 16.
